Variant 1:Adult. Suspected diffuse lung disease. Initial Imaging.
E. CT chest without IV contrast high-resolution
Numerous studies demonstrate increased sensitivity and specificity of CT over chest radiography in
the detection and characterization of DLD [26, 34, 35, 37, 40, 41, 44, 45, 47, 53]. Careful assessment
of the distribution of findings and morphological features on HRCT allow characterization of the
imaging pattern of DLD. A pattern-based approach on HRCT is often sufficient to make a confident
diagnosis or to narrow down the differential diagnosis. HRCT plays a central role in the diagnostic
algorithm of multiple current clinical guidelines [1, 16, 17, 54]. Imaging pattern characterization on
HRCT is especially important in the differentiation of usual interstitial pneumonia from other DLD
patterns as this carries diagnostic, therapeutic, and prognostic implications [1, 13, 17, 54-63].
Incorporation of HRCT interpretation into multidisciplinary discussions of DLD results in improved
diagnostic accuracy and confidence [13-16, 64-68]. In cases where diagnostic confidence remains
low—despite HRCT and multidisciplinary evaluation—tissue confirmation may be required and the
location of imaging abnormalities on HRCT may help guide appropriate biopsy sites [25, 54].
Adequate correlation is reported between CT disease extent and severity of symptoms and
physiologic testing for several DLD [39, 69-74]. The presence and extent of HRCT imaging features
of DLD may also serve as important prognostic variables [75].
